Population increased in Wrexham

The estimated population of Wrexham in 2024 was 138,245 usual residents, a rise of 1.0% since 2023.

This meant that Wrexham's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Wrexham increased by 2.3%.

Over this slightly longer period, Wrexham was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Wrexham

The average (median) age stayed at 42.8 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Wrexham has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Wrexham is an area that is classed as intermediate urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Wrexham's population of 138,245 usual residents was made up of:

  • 24,653 people aged 0 to 15 years, (17.8%)
  • 84,862 people aged 16 to 64 years, (61.4%)
  • 28,730 people aged 65 years and over, (20.8%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Wrexham has a slightly higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (20.8% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Wrexham, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Wrexham
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Wrexham, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 209 people (-0.2%). In total, there were 1,242 births and 1,451 deaths in Wrexham.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 446 (0.3%). There were 4,482 people entering the area and 4,036 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Wrexham's population of 1,057 (0.8%) as a result of 1,386 people entering the area and 329 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Wrexham was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Wrexham in mid-2023 is 136,890.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 662 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 79 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 741 people.
